chapter: Cafe Society and the Zodiac Suite
title: Hanging out on 52nd Street and jamming at her apartment
summary: Around 1946-47 she followed the new musicians on 52nd Street, and Tadd Dameron, Bud Powell, Miles Davis and others jammed at her apartment.

story.theme_name: Charlie Parker, Dizzy and the bebop revolution
story.community_name: Playing with and understanding Thelonious Monk

blocks.x: And then 5 years from then on into '46 and '47?
This was when bop was beginning to happen.
Bop happened a little later than that, about 2 years later, because Hazel went out and I went uptown. I began to follow -

Cafe Society uptown. He had both Cafe Society uptown, Barney Josephson did, and Cafe Society downtown. So I began hanging out on 52nd Street with the cats and they knew that I always helped musicians and so they'd - we'd come uptown around 4 o'clock or 4:30 in the morning and stay up all day, playing. There was Tadd Dameron, Bud Powell, Erroll Garner, Mel (Torme D'Armaine), and Miles Davis. Let's see, another trumpet player - Fats Navarro. A tenor man that was with Benny Goodman when he came out East - Wardell Gray, and sometimes Leonard Feather. I had a white rug on the floor and we'd sit on the floor and each one would take turns playing.
Oh, you played at your place, you mean?
But it wasn't jamming in the club or anything like that?
